chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Durust, from Ibrahim, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
"Whoever buys wheat, his wealth increases; and whoever buys flour, half of his wealth is lost; and whoever buys bread, all of his wealth is lost."
ai.seo_question: What is the economic wisdom behind buying wheat versus bread in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) to illustrate the economic principle that value diminishes as goods move from raw material to final consumption, reflecting the costs of labor and processing. This hadith is often cited in discussions of *Hukrah* (profiteering or hoarding) to warn against excessive markup in the food supply chain. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on fair pricing and the spiritual-economic link between simplicity in sustenance and preservation of wealth.
